title: Certified decoding of quantum LDPC codes
authors: Ragavi Krishnamoorthy, Florian Gerhardt, Johannes Knaute, Thomas Klir, Stefan Raimund Maschek, Erik Schulze, Tomislav Maras, Alexander Dotterweich, Loong Kuan Lee, Christian Bauckhage, Nico Piatkowski
abstract: Quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes reduce the qubit overhead of fault-tolerant quantum computation by an order of magnitude, but their decoding is harder than its classical counterpart: because many physical errors are equivalent up to stabilizers, the degenerate maximum-likelihood (ML) decoder must compare the probabilities of entire equivalence classes of errors, that is, partition functions, rather than single errors. The workhorse decoder BP+OSD sidesteps degeneracy heuristically and offers no guarantees. We treat degenerate decoding as probabilistic inference in an undirected graphical model: the probability of each logical class is the partition function of an unconstrained, strictly positive Markov random field over the code's check variables, a construction that generalizes the random-bond Ising mapping of the surface code to arbitrary CSS codes and to spacetime decoding with measurement errors and circuit-level noise. On this model we build two decoders. The first estimates all class partition functions by annealed importance sampling with common random numbers and attaches to every decision a certificate of optimality: a paired bootstrap test, or, composed with constant-factor estimators such as WISH, an exact optimality proof. The second is region-based: the Bethe free energy, whose bias cancels between classes, reproduces exact ML decoding on every tested surface-code instance at millisecond cost, and enlarging the regions to elimination clusters makes exact degenerate ML decoding of the [[72,12,6]] bivariate bicycle code feasible. Across surface codes and the bivariate bicycle codes [[72,12,6]] and [[144,12,12]], under code-capacity, phenomenological, and circuit-level noise, the sampling decoder matches or exceeds BP+OSD while certifying the bulk of its decisions, and the certificate flags exactly the syndromes on which any fast decoder should be distrusted.
summary: This work tackles the difficult problem of decoding quantum LDPC codes by reformulating it as estimating partition functions within a Markov Random Field model. The authors introduce novel, certified decoders that surpass existing heuristic methods by providing mathematical guarantees of optimality for most decisions. This advances the practical feasibility of fault-tolerant quantum computation by improving error correction decoding.
main_problem: The primary challenge is decoding quantum Low-Density Parity-Check (qLDPC) codes, which is significantly harder than classical decoding because errors are equivalent up to stabilizers, requiring the comparison of entire error class probabilities (partition functions).
main_result: The authors developed a certified sampling decoder that matches or exceeds existing decoders while providing formal certificates of optimality for the majority of syndrome decisions.
method: The problem is reframed as probabilistic inference in an undirected graphical model (Markov Random Field) over the code's check variables, allowing for the estimation of class partition functions using techniques like Annealed Importance Sampling (AIS) and Bethe free energy approximations.
model_or_system: The system is quantum error correction using qLDPC codes, which are treated as an MRF. The framework generalizes concepts from the surface code to arbitrary CSS codes and spacetime decoding.
key_observables: Logical error rates, certified fractions of correct decisions, and the comparison of decoding performance against heuristic decoders like BP+OSD.
important_parameters: Code structure (e.g., [[72, 12, 6]]), noise models (depolarizing, circuit-level), and the computational cost (e.g., millisecond decoding time).
main_assumptions: The core assumption is that the problem can be mapped to an MRF partition function estimation, and the Bethe decoder's bias cancels out when comparing different error classes.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the difficulty of degenerate quantum decoding, proposes the MRF framework for partition function estimation, details two main decoders (certified sampling and region-based), and validates them across various codes and noise models, concluding with hardware implementation results.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical framework for handling error degeneracy in quantum codes, especially the development of certified decoding methods, provides tools applicable to understanding the limits of fault-tolerant quantum computation.

(a) Absolute error of log ˆZλ versus the number of AIS sweeps T: the error decays as roughly T −1 and is ≈0.1 nats at T = 32. (b) Standard deviation of the error of the class log-ratio log ˆZ0 −log ˆZ1: common random numbers dominate in- dependent randomness uniformly in T (variance reduc- tion 1.2×–2.2×, growing with T).

Figure 3: Block logical error rates on the bivariate bi- cycle codes (Wilson 95% intervals; zero-failure points at p = 0.01 omitted from the log axis, see Table 1). On [[72, 12, 6]] the three decoders are statistically in- distinguishable; on the gross code BP+OSD-CS-7 re- tains an edge over both BP+OSD-0 and the (candidate- restricted) AIS decoder.

Figure 2: Logical error rate versus physical bit-flip rate on rotated surface codes (d = 3 left, d = 5 right; Wilson 95% intervals). The BP+OSD-0, MWPM, and exact- ML curves coincide to within statistical resolution at these distances; the AIS decoder (dashed) reproduces the decisions of the exact degenerate ML decoder al- most perfectly (see text). Plain BP fails at all rates, as expected from the degenerate posterior of Section 6.
